english.title: Adult attempt to engage in sexual communication with a child
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being a person aged 18 or over, for the purpose of obtaining sexual gratification, intentionally attempted to communicate with **(..NAME / REFERENCE OF CHILD..), a person under 16 who you did not reasonably believe to be 16 or over, the communication being

(A)_[sexual,]_
(B)_[intended to encourage him to make a communication that was sexual,]_
(C)_[intended to encourage her to make a communication that was sexual,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY THE NATURE AND CONTENT OF THE COMMUNICATION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
person aged 18 or over
for the purpose of obtaining sexual gratification
intentionally attempted to communicate with a person under 16
who they did not reasonably believe to be 16 or over
the communication being sexual / intended to encourage recipient to make sexual communication

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) For the purposes of this offence, a communication is sexual if any part of it relates to sexual activity, or a reasonable person would, in all the circumstances but regardless of any person's purpose, consider any part of the communication to be sexual.
(ii) In note (i) above, sexual activity means an activity that a reasonable person would, in all the circumstances but regardless of any person's purpose, consider to be sexual.
(iii) Section 1(2) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981 states that 'A person may be guilty of attempting to commit an offence to which this section applies even though the facts are such that the commission of the offence is impossible'.

other.penalty:
Either way -
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and / or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and / or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2002; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 15A(3)(a) of the Sexual Offences Act 2003 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2020.

Time limit on prosecutions:
None
